stemMd: In an aqueous phospholipid bilayer, which arrangement is most stable?

options.label: A
options.textMd: All heads face only the external solution.

options.label: B
options.textMd: All lipid molecules dissolve independently in water.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Phospholipids form a single covalent sheet.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Tails face water and heads meet at the centre.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Hydrophilic heads face water and hydrophobic tails face the bilayer interior.

explanationMd: Phospholipids are amphipathic. Burying tails away from water while exposing polar heads on both surfaces explains the bilayer's organisation and its barrier to many charged solutes.

distractorRationale.d: This exposes hydrophobic groups to water.
distractorRationale.c: Bilayer organisation does not require covalent linking between lipids.
distractorRationale.a: Both sides of a membrane contact water.
